content.rendered:
Bruce has gifted several songs to Southside Johnny over the years, but he also contributed in small ways on songs that Southside wrote himself.

Case in point: “Trapped Again,” a Southside Johnny composition from 1978, but one that that contains “bits and pieces” from Bruce and Steve (including Steve’s backing vocals).

Somehow, though, despite all the times they’ve performed together, it took Bruce and Southside more than two decades to finally play “Trapped Again” together–and that performance remains the one and only time Bruce has played the song.

Listen to that performance here, from Bruce’s guest appearance at Southside’s show at The Stone Pony on May 27, 2001:

Trapped Again
First performed: May 27, 2001 (Asbury Park, NJ)
Last performed: May 27, 2001 (Asbury Park, NJ)

© December 23, 2018

excerpt.rendered: Bruce co-wrote “Trapped Again” with Southside Johnny and Steve Van Zandt, but he’s only performed it live once. Check it out inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Chain of Fools
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce joins Southside Johnny and Graham Parker to cover one of Aretha Franklin's greatest hits.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Keep A-Knockin’
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce took a few runs at Little Richard's "Keep A-Knockin'." Listen to two of them here: one with Midnight Thunder, the other with Southside Johnny and The Asbury Jukes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Little by Little
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Southside Johnny took ill and couldn't perform, Little Steven saved the day by assembling an All-Star Revue to cover Junior Wells' classic "Little By Little."

jetpack-related-posts.title: Southside Shuffle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce turns the spotlight on Southside Johnny when Dr. Zoom and the Sonic Boom play the only known performance of "Southside Shuffle."

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ain’t That Peculiar
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Southside Johnny fronts The Bruce Springsteen Band on Marvin Gaye's Motown classic, but it's David Sancious who steals the show.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Down in the Valley
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce covers Solomon Burke's country soul classic with Southside Johnny and The Asbury Jukes in 1977.
